medications.purpose: Current antihypertensive monotherapy; part of combination therapy per NICE
medications.nice_justification: NG136 step 1 CCB for patients ≥55 y or as component of ACE‑I/CCB combination

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily in the morning
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; titrate to 5 mg after 2‑4 weeks, then up to 10 mg as tolerated
medications.purpose: Add to amlodipine to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg (NG136 step 2 combination therapy)
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends ACE‑I + CCB combination when monotherapy insufficient

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP, renal function and serum potassium 1‑2 weeks after start and after each dose increase

contraindications.reason: Potential teratogenicity; ACE‑I contraindicated in pregnancy (NG136)
contraindications.alternative: If pregnant or planning pregnancy, use labetalol or methyldopa

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²; renal function will be checked before starting ACE‑I and after dose changes
Pregnancy status unknown – must be confirmed before initiating ramipril
Allergy status to ACE‑I/ARB not documented – verify no history of angio‑edema
QRISK cardiovascular risk assessment not available – to be performed at next visit to guide lipid management
treatment_summary: The patient is a young adult female with stage 2 hypertension on low‑dose amlodipine. Per NICE NG136, add ramipril 2.5 mg daily to create an ACE‑I/CCB combination, titrating to the maximum tolerated dose to reach target BP <140/90 mmHg. Continue amlodipine. Monitor BP, renal function and electrolytes after initiation and dose changes, and confirm pregnancy status before starting. Review therapy annually and consider adding a thiazide‑like diuretic (e.g., indapamide) if BP remains uncontrolled.
